newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Elections won't hurt Brazil's fiscal drive - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Elections won't hurt Brazil's fiscal drive - Malan.

text.p: Next year's elections in Brazil will not distract the government from its drive to keep a grip on inflation and public spending, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said Wednesday.
"The only thing we want is long-term, sustainable growth," Malan told a news conference. "The fact that 1998 is an election year does not alter in any way the government's decisions."
Typically, public spending rises during election years as a result of campaigning and last-minute public works spending.
But Malan said there would be no attempt by the government to increase Brazil's rate of growth and boost the re-election chances of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Brazil holds elections in October next year to choose a new president, state governors and much of Congress.
The minister also responded to critics of the government who have questioned the wisdom of its policy of high interest rates and a strong currency.
"There is no problem in keeping the program until the end of 1998 (when the government's term ends)," Malan said. "We don't have to do anything different to what we're already doing."
